text:
maria: Heads up — seeing a burst of ECC/Xid events in us-west-2 after last night's kernel roll. dcgm-exporter showing 40+ card-level ECC spikes across 4 nodes in ~30m. Alerts are noisy and repeating.
sam: Do we have the panels/queries? Which metric are we looking at — dcgm_ecc_single_bit or exporter_raw_xid_count?
maria: Grafana link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/xyz/gpu-health — spikes on dcgm_ecc_single_bit_total and a corresponding dcgm_xid_last_seen_count bump around 02:14-02:40 UTC.
kai: I checked the node image history — the 4 nodes were rolled to kernel 6.1.12 and driver 535.54 last night. I've seen driver/firmware combos cause transient ECC/XID noise on A100s.
alex: Oncall suggested draining the worst offenders, but we shouldn't mass-drain if it's alert flapping. Current prometheus rule pages on any single ECC event which is too sensitive for noisy windows.
dcgm-bot: [alert] gpu_ecc_unhealthy firing for gpu-node-uw2-3,gpu-node-uw2-7,gpu-node-uw2-12,gpu-node-uw2-19 — alert_id=ALERT-2026-07-15-001
maria: Proposal: tune the prom rule to focus on sustained activity, e.g. require increase(dcgm_ecc_single_bit_total[10m]) > 3 OR count_over_time(dcgm_xid_detected[10m]) > 2 and add a `for: 15m` before paging. Also add a label-based suppression for nodes with recent kernel/driver rolls so we avoid noisy post-roll pages.
sam: +1 to the sustained-window approach. Also propose adding a small grace period when the cluster lifecycle job labels nodes with `rolling=true` so alerts auto-suppress while kernel jobs finish.
kai: Quick POC I ran locally:
```
- alert: GPU_ECC_Noise
  expr: increase(dcgm_ecc_single_bit_total[10m]) > 3
  for: 15m
  labels:
    severity: warning
    hypothesis: noisy-driver
```
This eliminated the single-event pages in the 02:00-03:00 window while still surfacing sustained failures.
alex: Sounds good. Operationally we'll still drain any node with XID > 5 over 1h or repeated ECC rate > 10/hour on multiple cards. I'll open a short RFC to 1) change the rule, 2) add lifecycle label-based suppression, 3) add the drain thresholds.
oncall-ops: I'm fine with tuning rules to reduce paging. Two asks: 1) add an automated synthetic probe (small cuda job) that runs after drain/reboot to verify driver/card recovery before returning node to schedulers, and 2) track these noisy-driver incidents in the gpu-health incident board for trend analysis. If the POC reduces noise, we'll roll to prod tonight. :thumbsup:
